name: Eritrea
summary_text: Eritrea is a place trans visitors should avoid entirely. Article 310(1) of the 2015 Penal Code criminalises “homosexual conduct” (up to 7 years), there are no anti-discrimination protections of any kind, and Eritrea is among the world's most closed states — indefinite national service, mass arbitrary detention, no independent media, no civil society, and no way to document conditions. Eritrea has rejected every SOGI recommendation at every UPR cycle. Nothing is known about trans people in Eritrea because nothing can be known — the absence of data reflects total informational control.

sources.claim_summary: NOTE: Not retrievable at research time (HTTP 403); the underlying Human Dignity Trust country profile documents that Eritrea criminalises same-sex sexual activity (up to 7 years' imprisonment).

sources.title: Eritrea | Outright International
sources.claim_summary: Outright International country overview (updated March 2026): Article 310(1) of the 2015 penal code criminalises 'homosexual conduct' with up to 7 years' imprisonment (inherited from the 1957 Ethiopian code, sentence enhanced at independence). No SOGISC protections; the 2023 US State Department report noted coerced conversion practices to avoid imprisonment and grossly restricted freedoms; no LGBTIQ organisations; queer people remain closeted for fear of imprisonment and violence.

sources.title: Eritrea - United States Department of State
sources.claim_summary: US State Department 2023 Human Rights Report for Eritrea: official assessment including the SOGI section - Article 310 criminalises same-sex conduct (up to 7 years), coerced conversion practices reported, grossly restricted freedoms.

US State Department 2010 Human Rights Report for Eritrea (archived): documents the authoritarian regime's abuses - torture, arbitrary detention, indefinite national service - with the LGBT section noting criminalisation and societal stigma.

sources.title: [AIM] Asmarino Independent Media - Eritrea: US State Department Report on Human Rights for 2011
sources.claim_summary: Asmarino Independent Media (June 2012): reproduction of the US State Department 2011 Human Rights Report for Eritrea - authoritarian rule under President Afwerki, consistent serious human-rights violations, security forces acting with impunity; includes the LGBT section.

sources.title: Eritrea - Country of Concern - GOV.UK
sources.claim_summary: UK FCO 'Eritrea - Country of Concern' report (updated Jan 2015): covers elections, freedom of expression, human-rights defenders, access to justice, death penalty, torture, and freedom of religion - official UK assessment of the human-rights environment.
